interpretation: A larger input reservoir and startup reserve improve resilience to bounded producer pauses. The 30-ms full-stream model does not reproduce hardware picture 348; a 45-ms cold-start dense excerpt does produce a gap on that source picture plus two others, all removed by the combined simulation experiment. This supports a hardware-validation candidate, not an exact recovery of host traffic or a proven hardware fix.
limitations: Behavioral FIFO pointer visibility is not a cycle-exact Intel primitive or metastability model.
Host data are synthetic 16-bit transfers at 20 MHz with configurable stride and post-full resume pauses; the real host schedule is unknown.
DDR is ideal except the separate periodic-busy control; physical arbitration/read contention and HDMI raster/scaler are absent.
Reconstructed-sample order/location/value fingerprints are compared across variants, not against a new independent decoder oracle.
Repeated-session tests reset the entire modeled pipeline and FIFO, not the full warm-load/download-rearm or Bob/Weave interaction paths.

STARTUP_WINDOWS counts raw frame windows after first completion; in the tested phases two suppressions postpone the first actual swap by one frame. Production startup must be based on readiness and clean display/timeline release, not blindly copied raw-window counting.
Startup reserve moves the early hold into startup; it does not accelerate decoding or shorten the tested full-stream completion time.
No FPGA source, constraints, active MiSTer image or display settings changed; no Quartus build or hardware acceptance was performed.
